Subject: Update on Saturday’s tenant clinic

We understand why people are concerned. Receiving a lawyer’s letter after asking for help can be frightening, and it’s reasonable to want clear answers about how information is handled.

Cascade Legal Rights Project does not provide clinic attendee information to landlords or their attorneys, and we do not sell or disclose it. Sign-in records are kept internally in locked storage. We can’t speak to any individual’s situation in this thread. In general, eviction filings in Magistrate Court are public records, and some firms use those records to send mailings. A letter arriving after someone attends a clinic does not, by itself, show that the clinic shared their information.

The free walk-in tenant rights clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. The library meeting room is closed, so we’ve moved the clinic to Mt. Zion Fellowship Hall in East Atlanta. The side entrance by the parking lot is accessible. No appointment is needed, and everyone is still welcome.

If you have questions, email clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. We appreciate people raising concerns and want everyone to have the information they need to decide whether to attend.
